'''Joseph Henri''' "'''Josy'''" '''Barthel'''<ref name="SR">{{cite Sports-Reference |title=Josy Barthel |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ba/josy-barthel-1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161202214908/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ba/josy-barthel-1.html |archive-date=2 December 2016}}</ref> (24 April 1927 &ndash; 7 July 1992) was a [[Luxembourgers|Luxembourgish]] [[Athletics (sport)|athlete]] and politician.  He was the surprise winner of the Men's [[1500 metres]] at the [[1952 Summer Olympics]], and the only athlete representing Luxembourg to have won a [[gold medal]] at the Olympics.<ref>Luxembourger [[Michel Théato]] won the [[marathon]] in [[1900 Summer Olympics|1900]], but the IOC officially credits him as having represented France, despite later research proving his nationality.</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Barthel emerges from under middle-distance radar |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/barthel-emerges-from-under-middle-distance-radar |website=Olympics.com |access-date=16 August 2021}}</ref>  Besides athletics, Barthel also led successful careers in both chemistry and politics.

==Biography==
Born in [[Mamer]], Josy Barthel's abilities as a [[Middle distance track event|middle-distance runner]] were discovered during [[World War II]]. His first fame came by winning the 800 m at the Military World Championships in [[Berlin]] in 1947. The next year at Military World Championships in [[Brussels]] he won both 800 m and 1500 m.

At the [[1948 Summer Olympics]] in [[London]], Barthel finished ninth at the 1500 m final. Then he won Student World Championships in 1949 (1500 m) and 1951 (800 m and 1500 m).  The absolute high point of Barthel's career was the [[1952 Summer Olympics]], where he surprised the crowd and himself by winning the 1500 m with a very strong finish. He also participated at the [[1956 Summer Olympics]], after which he retired from running. He was also Luxembourg champion in 800 m and 1500 m from 1946 to 1956.

In 1962 Barthel became the president of the [[Luxembourg Athletics Federation]], then from 1973 to 1977 he was the president of the [[Luxembourgish Olympic and Sporting Committee]]. A member of the Democratic Party, he later entered politics, serving as a minister from 1977 to 1984 in the [[Thorn-Vouel-Berg Government|Thorn-Vouel-Berg]] and [[Werner-Thorn-Flesch Government|Werner-Thorn-Flesch]] governments.

Josy Barthel died in [[Luxembourg City]] after a severe illness.

The former national stadium of Luxembourg, home until September 2021 to the [[Luxembourg national football team|national football team]], was named [[Stade Josy Barthel]] in his honor. The [[Lycée Technique Josy Barthel]] in Mamer also bears his name.

In 2006, Barthel was accused of [[doping (sport)|doping]] by sports journalist Erik Eggers in the [[Germany|German]] newspaper ''[[Der Tagesspiegel]].''<ref>{{cite news |first=Erik |last=Eggers |title=Mit der Kraft der Panzerschokolade &#124; Olympiasieger Joseph Barthel soll 1952 gedopt haben |url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/mit-der-kraft-der-panzerschokolade-1412545.html |newspaper=[[Der Tagesspiegel]] |date=26 November 2006 |access-date=23 July 2026 |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080818003950/http://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/;art272,2229157 |archive-date=18 August 2008 |url-status=live}}</ref> Eggers cited German physician Oskar Wegener who did research on [[methamphetamine]] and other doping substances in the 1950s. Wegener strongly denied saying Barthel had any connection with doping.<ref>{{cite news |title=Enkelin verteidigt Barthel gegen Vorwürfe |url=http://www.wort.lu/articles/5768386.html |publisher=[[Luxemburger Wort]] |date=29 November 2006 |access-date=5 August 2008 |language=de |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080129092623/http://www.wort.lu/articles/5768386.html |archive-date=29 January 2008}}</ref> The use of such substances was neither prohibited nor controlled until the 1960s.<ref>{{cite news |title=Es gibt keinen Dopingfall Barthel |url=http://www.wort.lu/articles/5768388.html |publisher=[[Luxemburger Wort]] |date=28 November 2006 |access-date=5 August 2008 |language=de |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070915074658/http://www.wort.lu/articles/5768388.html |archive-date=15 September 2007}}</ref>
